memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Do not deny justice to your poor people in their lawsuits. Have nothing to do with a false charge and do not put an innocent or honest person to death, for I will not acquit the guilty." - Exodus 23:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God returns to His deep concern for justice, and here He guards the vulnerable and the innocent. Do not deny the poor a fair hearing simply because they lack power. Stay far away from false accusations. And never let an innocent person be condemned. Then God adds a sobering line about Himself: "I will not acquit the guilty." The God who commands justice from us is Himself perfectly just.

Notice how God insists on justice for the poor here, having just warned against favouring the poor unfairly. Together these commands paint a full picture: justice must be truly even. The poor must not be cheated because they are weak, nor favoured merely because they are poor. Truth and fairness apply to all. God's standard never bends toward power or away from it — it simply seeks what is right.

And behind all our striving for justice stands the God who is Justice itself. He will not let the guilty go free forever, and He will not let the innocent be forgotten. This is both a warning and a comfort. A warning, because we cannot hide our own guilt from Him. A comfort, because every injustice we suffer or witness will one day be set right by His perfect hand. And wonderfully, the cross is where God's justice and mercy meet — where the guilty can be acquitted, not by ignoring justice, but by Christ satisfying it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I defend fair treatment for those too weak to defend themselves?
How does it comfort me that God will ultimately set every injustice right?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are perfectly just and will set every wrong right. Help me defend the vulnerable and love the truth, and thank You that at the cross the guilty find mercy. Amen.
